candidates.tagline: Google Japan built a keyboard where the keys scroll to your fingers — firmware marked TBD
candidates.story: Google Japan released an open-source concept keyboard where 116 keys ride on 4 continuous conveyor belts rotating toward the user's fingers so you never move your hand, but the firmware section for actually sending key presses to a computer is marked 'TBD.'
candidates.why_funny: The solution to not wanting to move your fingers is an elaborate conveyor system — and it doesn't even fully work yet.
candidates.alt: Blue keyboard with four rows of mechanical keys mounted on conveyor belts, a hand reaching toward the scrolling keys

candidates.tagline: Every microwave has a Popcorn button. Every bag of microwave popcorn says don't use it.
candidates.story: Hackaday surfaced why microwaves universally ship with a dedicated Popcorn button while every bag of microwave popcorn carries an explicit 'Do not use popcorn button' warning — because manufacturers implement it wildly differently, from a dumb timer to humidity sensors, so no popcorn maker can calibrate for all of them.
candidates.why_funny: The Popcorn button was designed to make popcorn perfectly; it's so inconsistent that the product specifically made for it warns you never to use it.
candidates.alt: Back of a ConAgra microwave popcorn bag with 'HELPFUL HINTS' section visibly reading 'Do not use popcorn button'
